name: Desire (kāma)
description: A person is made of desire; desire leads to resolve, action and its result, and the desiring one returns to this world for action (BAU 4.4.5-6); one who desires desires is born here and there by them (MuU 3.2.2); children pursue outward desires into the net of death (KU 2.1.2); when all desires in the heart are released one becomes immortal (BAU 4.4.7; KU 2.3.14).
antidotes: knowing the self as one's only desire (āptakāma, ātmakāma, BAU 4.4.6)

name: Ignorance (avidyā)
description: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): fools living in ignorance and thinking themselves wise go round like the blind led by the blind (KU 1.2.5; MuU 1.2.8); the knot of ignorance (MuU 2.1.10); the teacher takes one across to the far shore of ignorance (PrU 6.8).

name: The knots of the heart
description: Knots in the heart that bind one to mortality; when they are cut, all doubts vanish and one's actions are exhausted, and the mortal becomes immortal (KU 2.3.15; MuU 2.2.8, 3.2.9); loosened by firm memory arising from pure food and mind (ChU 7.26.2).
antidotes: seeing the higher and the lower (MuU 2.2.8)

name: Choosing the pleasant over the good
description: The fool chooses the pleasant (preyas) for the sake of getting and keeping; the child deluded by wealth thinks 'this is the world, there is no other' and falls again into Death's power (KU 1.2.2, 1.2.6).
antidotes: discerning the good from the pleasant, as Naciketas did (KU 1.1.21-29)

name: Heedlessness (pramāda)
description: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'do not neglect truth, dharma, study' (TU 1.11); the target is to be pierced by one who is undistracted (MuU 2.2.4); not attained through heedlessness (MuU 3.2.4); in yoga one becomes undistracted (KU 2.3.11).

name: Doubt (saṃśaya)
description: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): Śāṇḍilya's meditation succeeds for one who has 'no doubt' (ChU 3.14.4); when he is seen all doubts are cut (MuU 2.2.8); free from doubt he becomes a brahmin (BAU 4.4.23); Naciketas's doubt about the dead (KU 1.1.20).

name: Evil (pāpman)
description: Evil pierced the senses in the gods' contest, so that one speaks, sees and thinks what is improper (BAU 1.3; ChU 1.2); evils turn back from the self, the dam (ChU 8.4); the knower's evils burn like a reed tuft (ChU 5.24.3), do not cling like water on a lotus leaf (ChU 4.14.3); the self is free from evil (ChU 8.1.5).

name: Taking the body to be the self
description: Virocana concludes from the teaching of the reflected person that the body is the self and teaches the asuras to worship and adorn the body — 'the doctrine of the asuras'; Indra sees that such a self perishes with the body (ChU 8.7-8.9).
antidotes: continued inquiry with a teacher (Indra's 101 years, ChU 8.7-12)
notes: The Sanskrit compound dehātmabuddhi is later Vedānta usage; the ChU describes the view without naming it.

name: Fear (bhaya)
description: Fear arises from a second (BAU 1.4.2); when one makes the slightest gap in brahman there is fear (TU 2.7); the knower of brahman's bliss is never afraid (TU 2.4, 2.9); brahman is fearlessness (BAU 4.4.25).
antidotes: knowing the one without a second

name: Sorrow (śoka)
description: Nārada, knowing only mantras, is in sorrow; 'the knower of the self crosses sorrow' (ChU 7.1.3; MuU 3.2.9); for one who sees oneness there is no delusion or sorrow (Īśa 7); the wise leaves joy and sorrow (KU 1.2.12); seeing the Lord the grieving bird is freed from sorrow (MuU 3.1.2).

name: Hunger, thirst, sorrow, delusion, old age and death
description: The self within all is beyond hunger and thirst, sorrow and delusion, old age and death (BAU 3.5.1); the self free from evil is without old age, death, sorrow, hunger and thirst (ChU 8.1.5, 8.7.1).
notes: The name 'six waves' (ṣaḍūrmi) is later Vedānta usage (moderate).

name: The three desires (for sons, wealth and worlds)
description: Knowers of the self rise above the desire for sons, the desire for wealth and the desire for worlds and live as mendicants; 'the desire for sons is the desire for wealth, and the desire for wealth is the desire for worlds' (BAU 3.5.1, 4.4.22).

name: Pride of the gods
description: The gods, taking brahman's victory for their own, grew proud; they could not recognize the yakṣa until Umā revealed that it was brahman (Kena 3.1-4.1).
antidotes: knowledge that the victory is brahman's (Kena 4.1)

name: The marks of tamas and rajas (Maitrī 3.5)
description: MaiU 3.5 lists the marks of tamas (delusion, fear, despondency, sleep, sloth, heedlessness, old age, grief, hunger, thirst...) and of rajas (craving, affection, passion, greed, violence, lust, hatred, deceit...), with which the elemental self is filled.
antidotes: knowledge, austerity and one's own dharma (MaiU 4.3)
